response.query: Which risk-of-bias tools will we use for each study design (RCT, cohort, cross-sectional, qualitative) and how will we grade overall certainty (GRADE or adapted framework) for predictor-level conclusions?
response.answer: For RCTs, use Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool; for cohorts, use NIH Quality Assessment Tool; for cross-sections, use same NIH tool; for qualitative, use CASP Checklist; overall certainty graded with GRADE.

results.title: Methodological Standards for Conducting High-Quality ...
results.content: Essential data typically extracted include study identifiers (authors, year, journal), study design (e.g., RCT, cohort, case-control), population characteristics (e.g., sample size, demographics), intervention and comparator details, outcomes measured and timepoints, results (e.g., effect sizes, confidence intervals), funding sources, and potential conflicts of interest Similarly to the study screening and selection process, data extraction should be performed independently by at least two researchers, as evidence indicates that relying on a single extractor can lead to 21% more errors compared to a double-extraction approach [25].
